record_title: Time-varying rates gauge away constant parameters in the Moose-Wolf inverse model
provenance: A source-specific structural-identifiability correction for the non-autonomous Holling type-II and ratio-dependent Moose-Wolf inverse models in arXiv:2609.20793v1. Explicit gauge transformations show that unknown time-dependent growth and death rates can exactly absorb changes in the constant interaction parameters while preserving the complete observed trajectory.
limitations: The result concerns the non-autonomous ODE when alpha(t) and delta(t) are unknown time-varying functions. It does not analyze a separately declared finite-dimensional neural-network parameterization of those functions, nor does it invalidate numerical trajectory fits. The full three-constant gauge requires regular intervals with x^4 != 1, although nonidentifiability of c persists without that condition. General unknown-input identifiability theory is established prior literature; originality is restricted to the explicit source-specific obstruction and its consequences.
